## Verdict

**Acme Desk** costs least for a team of 35, at **$280 per month**. It has both the lowest per-seat rate ($8) and a minimum (10 seats) well below the team size, so all 35 seats bill at list with no padding. Fennel HQ is next at $420; Kelp is the most expensive at $850, inflated by a 50-seat minimum that forces payment for 15 seats the team will not use.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Acme Desk | $8 | 10 |
| Fennel HQ | $12 | 25 |
| Kelp | $17 | 50 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 35 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Acme Desk:** minimum 10 < 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $8 = **$280 per month**. Effective rate $8.00 per person.
- **Fennel HQ:** minimum 25 < 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $12 = **$420 per month**. Effective rate $12.00 per person.
- **Kelp:** minimum 50 > 35, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $17 = **$850 per month**. Effective rate $24.29 per person ($850 ÷ 35) — 15 unused seats worth $255 per month.

Acme Desk is $140 per month cheaper than Fennel HQ and $570 per month cheaper than Kelp. Over twelve months that is $1,680 and $6,840 respectively.

## Risks

Kelp's penalty is a minimum-seat artefact and disappears at 50 people, where its effective rate drops to $17. Even then it does not overtake Acme Desk on list price at any size, since Acme Desk's $8 rate is lowest and its minimum is already cleared. Acme Desk stays cheapest as the team grows or shrinks to 10; below 10 people its $80 floor applies.

This comparison covers list price only. The price list states nothing about features, support tiers, usage caps, security posture, or integrations, so a cheaper seat may buy less product — that gap is unmeasured here.

All figures assume monthly billing at list, as stated. Annual commitments, volume discounts, onboarding fees, and switching or migration costs are not in the source and could change the totals. Confirm whether minimums are enforced only at signup or at every renewal.
